observation.visible_scene: A near-still, misty water surface viewed from above. The water mirrors an orange-brown leafy canopy across the top, dark-green trees along the right edge, a broad pale gray reflection filling the center, and two small pale vertical marks at the lower-left. A tiny bright speck sits near the middle of the frame throughout.
visible_changes: The reflected tree shapes and the gray central reflection continuously wobble and deform in small amounts, consistent with gentle surface ripples rather than the objects themselves moving.
The orange canopy reflection at the top shifts and breaks up slightly frame-to-frame, and the green tree reflections on the right similarly ripple and distort.
The small bright speck near the center stays at roughly the same position, drifting only by a few pixels with minor jitter across the segment; it does not travel across the frame.
The two pale vertical marks at the lower-left remain fixed in place, changing only in slight blur/shape as the water surface moves.
No large-scale scene translation occurs; the overall layout of reflections is preserved from first to last frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produces the ripples (wind, an unseen object, etc.) is not shown.
The identity and material of the central speck and of the lower-left marks are not determinable from the reflections alone.
Any motion before the first frame or after the last frame is outside this excerpt.
uncertain_details: Camera motion cannot be confirmed; the apparent small shifts are most consistent with water-surface deformation, but a very slight camera drift cannot be ruled out.
Whether the central speck is a floating object or a reflection/highlight is ambiguous.
The exact cause of the ripple pattern is inferred, not observed.
